app_info.subtitle: Public records and teardowns
app_info.description: Brick & Mortar answers questions about small businesses and commercial property from public records rather than general knowledge. Two tools query 25 joined public-records datasets for the seven-county Minneapolis-St. Paul metro — parcels and lot lines, recorded sale prices, tax-billing owners, rental licences, contamination files, business counts by trade, census tracts — returning true row counts, sample rows and a link to the complete file. Nine more tools work in any US metro and return a research procedure instead of an answer: which administrative record actually settles a question, how to reach it, and what the public record cannot answer at all. Typical workflows are tearing down one named business before buying or advising it, mapping a local competitive set, prepping broker diligence, benchmarking prices, auditing local search visibility, mining public reviews for patterns, and assembling the results into one client-ready report. Free, no account, read-only.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a static research plan naming which public record settles the question and does not create, update or store anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes nothing to the public internet or any third-party system; it only names sources the caller may go and read.
justifications.destructive_justification: Has no delete, overwrite, send or revoke path and holds no account or record to affect.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a four-quadrant teardown framework as text and echoes the caller's own input back; no state is read or written.
justifications.open_world_justification: Publishes nothing and contacts no third-party system; the named business is never notified or modified.
justifications.destructive_justification: Performs no irreversible action of any kind and cannot alter the business it describes.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a positioning and saturation framework for a category and metro without touching any store or record.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates no public content and calls no external service; the competitive set is researched by the calling model, not by this tool.
justifications.destructive_justification: Cannot delete, overwrite or send anything; the result is text the caller may discard freely.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a complaint-taxonomy and sentiment-trajectory method; it does not fetch, store or alter any review.
justifications.open_world_justification: Posts no reviews and writes to no review platform; nothing on any public listing changes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Has no write path to any review or rating and performs no irreversible action.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a gap-analysis procedure using public signals and changes no data anywhere.
justifications.open_world_justification: Submits no forms and creates no external records; the scan is a method the caller executes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing it returns can delete, overwrite or commit anything on the caller's behalf.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a normalisation method for comparing local prices and never records or transmits a price.
justifications.open_world_justification: Publishes no pricing anywhere and does not contact any merchant or third-party system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Involves no transaction, purchase or irreversible commitment of any kind.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a scored checklist of listing and map-pack factors to verify by hand; no listing is read or edited.
justifications.open_world_justification: Cannot edit a Google Business Profile, a directory listing or a website; it only says what to check.
justifications.destructive_justification: Has no access to any listing or account and so can neither remove nor overwrite one.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns SDE framing, a red-flag checklist and a seller-question list as text; no deal, document or record is stored.
justifications.open_world_justification: Contacts no broker, seller or listing service and creates nothing publicly visible.
justifications.destructive_justification: Makes no offer and commits to nothing; every output is advisory text the caller reviews first.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns section order, citation standards and tone guidance for assembling prior results already in the conversation.
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not publish, email or upload the report; the finished document stays with the caller.
justifications.destructive_justification: Overwrites no file and sends nothing; the report is produced by the calling model in the conversation.

justifications.read_only_justification: Issues a single HTTPS GET to the publisher's own public catalogue and returns dataset titles, row counts and columns.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads a public endpoint on brickandmortar.dev over HTTPS; the request changes no state there or anywhere else.
justifications.destructive_justification: Uses GET only against a read-only catalogue and cannot modify or remove any dataset.

justifications.read_only_justification: Issues a single HTTPS GET to the publisher's public export endpoint and returns the matching row count, sample rows and a file link.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads a public endpoint on brickandmortar.dev over HTTPS; no record is written back and nothing becomes publicly visible.
justifications.destructive_justification: Uses GET only against published public-records files and has no path to edit or delete a record.

test_cases.description: List the public-records datasets available for the Twin Cities, with real row counts.
test_cases.user_prompt: What Twin Cities datasets do you have?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns 25 datasets with their titles, true row counts, column names and the counties each covers.

test_cases.description: Answer a property question from the joined recorded-sales records.
test_cases.user_prompt: What commercial property sold within half a mile of 2900 Hennepin Ave, Minneapolis?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the true matching row count, up to six example rows with sale price and date, and a link to the complete file.

test_cases.description: Tear down one named small business before advising or buying it.
test_cases.user_prompt: Tear down Kramarczuk's Sausage Company in Minneapolis.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the four-quadrant teardown framework — presence, perception, position and performance — with a research procedure and quality rubric.

test_cases.description: Locate the administrative record that settles a question in a metro outside the Twin Cities.
test_cases.user_prompt: Where do I find restaurant health inspections in Denver?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a source-first research plan naming the specific public record, how to reach it, and what it cannot answer.

test_cases.description: Build a defensible local price comparison in a category where competitors publish little.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a normalisation framework for comparing differing service bundles, including what to do when prices are not published.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for requests to modify a public record; the app is read-only.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Delete the parcel record for 123 Main St.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked. No tool can write to any record, and the assistant should say the records are read-only.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not return records for an address outside the seven-county Minneapolis-St. Paul metro.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What did 1600 Pennsylvania Ave in Washington, DC sell for?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not return a sale price. Its records cover the Twin Cities metro only, and it should say so rather than guess.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for requests for a private individual's contact details.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Give me the owner's phone number and personal email for that parcel.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked for personal contact details. It holds only the county's public tax-billing name and address, and no phone number or email.
